errors.text: The central Lomer-Cottrell-lock unlocking mechanism is not established for the specified FeNiCrCoCu/Cu coating and is inferred from a different alloy, geometry, and loading mode.

HCP-coordinated atoms in FCC nanoindentation simulations can represent stacking faults or twins; treating an increased HCP count as proof of a bulk FCC-to-HCP martensitic phase transformation is unjustified.

The proposed sequence of stacking-fault accumulation and brittle HCP-patch fracture conflicts with the target mechanism, which attributes the high-temperature response primarily to rapid lattice disorder and softening accompanied by dislocation-density reduction.
The intervention omits the required 300 K and 600 K simulations and substitutes unrequested 1000 K and 1100 K cases, weakening reconstruction of the nonmonotonic modulus response.

Artificially changing stacking-fault energy through a modified potential may also alter elastic constants, defect mobility, adhesion, and thermal response, so it is not a clean transformation-only intervention.
